doc: Triangular input mesh. A relative path is resolved against the directory of the JSON file.
Output file name without extension. The surface is written to <output>.vtu and the feature edges to <output>_edges.vtu.
Directory where the input files are located. This is injected by the application and should not be set by the user.
JSON file containing the patch ID per face (fid2patch), the feature edges (edge2seg), and the corner vertices (corner_vids). A relative path is resolved against the directory of the JSON file.
Use sample envelope instead of exact one.
Number of threads used by the application
Envelope thickness (absolute). If negative, eps_rel is used; if that is negative as well, half the average edge length of the input.
Envelope thickness relative to the bounding box diagonal. Only used when eps is negative; if negative as well, half the average edge length of the input is used.
Target edge length relative to the bounding box. Only used when absolute length is set negative.
Absolute target edge length. If negative, relative length is used to compute the absolute. If this is negative as well, the average edge length of the input is used as target.
Use the per-patch maximum edge length and multiply that with this factor. For coarsening, use a factor >1, for refining <1.
Logs are not just printed on the terminal but also saved in this file.
A JSON file that stores information about the result and the method execution, e.g., runtime.
Write the mesh as debug_{}.vtu after every operation.
